## ✨ Highlights

A cluster member can be recycled without losing its address, and a
cluster's Let's Encrypt is configured once, on the cluster.

- ♻️ **Recycling keeps the address**: a member with a static address is
  replaced by a new machine that takes that address over - the routers'
  BGP neighbours, firewall rules, NAT and monitoring keep pointing at
  the same address. Neighbours learn the change at once.
- 🔐 **Let's Encrypt managed by the cluster**: the mode, the
  certificates and the DNS providers are set on the **Clusters** page
  and are the same on every member, whichever member orders - with
  **Test**, **Renew** and an account key import there.
- 🖥️ **A Controller starting while GitHub is very slow** knows the
  releases within a minute or so, and a node's **Update** page shows an
  upload's progress.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Let's Encrypt on a cluster is opt-in.** A cluster keeps working as
  before until its Let's Encrypt is set on the cluster. From then on the
  members' Let's Encrypt configuration is **locked** like their
  HAProxy configuration: a change on a member is refused (`janusctl
  cluster release acme` frees it for an emergency, and the member is
  then reported as drifted). Every member must run this release for the
  cluster to take it over - an older member is refused before anything
  changes.
- **A version keepalived or BIRD refuses now fails the apply.** It was
  recorded as applied while the members kept their previous VRRP or BGP
  configuration: a cluster carrying such a version will report a
  failure on its next apply, with keepalived's or BIRD's message.
- **An apply touches only what changed on each member**: a version that
  changes Let's Encrypt only, or leaves a firewall ruleset as it was,
  no longer reloads HAProxy or puts the ruleset on trial again.
- **Nodes announce the addresses they add** (gratuitous ARP, unsolicited
  Neighbour Advertisement). Single addresses (`/32`, `/128`) are not
  announced. An address takeover works with nodes on older releases too,
  their neighbours just take longer to follow.

## 🧩 Clusters

- **Recycling keeps a member's address**
  ([#643](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/643),
  [#647](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/647), fixes
  [#515](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/515),
  [Keeping a member's address](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#keeping-a-members-address)):
  **It takes X's address** on the Recycle form, `keep_address` +
  `temporary_address` in the API, `janusctl cluster replace
  -keep-address`.
  - The newcomer joins **drained** on a temporary address. The member
    leaves and gives its address up: its machine is destroyed, or a node
    the Controller didn't make is powered off.
  - Once nothing answers at the old address, the newcomer takes it on
    trial and confirms it there. The Controller, the machine's record
    and the janusctl context follow the node; the released node is
    forgotten.
  - The cluster's version is applied again on **every** member (peers
    sections, keepalived's `unicast_src_ip`/`unicast_peer`), then the
    newcomer serves.
  - A member that only moves: **Address** on the member, `POST
    /api/clusters/{id}/members/{name}/address`, `janusctl cluster
    readdress`.
  - Refused before anything is touched: an address from DHCP, a
    cluster of one member, a cluster firewall whose rules depend on the
    member's own address (the message says what to change).
  - The moving member's keepalived stays out until the others name it
    by its new address: no two masters while it moves. The same held
    when a member joined, and is fixed too.
  - A move has 2 minutes to be confirmed (was 1), retried every second.
  - Proven on libvirt and on Proxmox VE: the member holding the virtual
    IP recycled in 83 s, 3 probes lost out of 435 (every 0.2 s) before
    the two fixes above.
- **Let's Encrypt as a cluster-managed domain**
  ([#644](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/644),
  [#645](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/645), fixes
  [#569](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/569),
  [Let's Encrypt](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#lets-encrypt)):
  a **Let's Encrypt** tab on the cluster, `PUT
  /api/clusters/{id}/letsencrypt`, `janusctl cluster letsencrypt`.
  - The configuration - how the CA is reached (direct, a proxy, the
    Controller's relay, ordered by the Controller), the certificates,
    the account's settings, the DNS providers - is part of the
    cluster's version, the same on every member. A change of the
    member that orders keeps the mode; every member is ready to order.
  - **Secrets never go in a version.** DNS providers' credentials, the
    EAB key and a proxy's password are handed to the member that orders
    and pulled from it by the others, member to member: the Controller
    keeps none of them.
  - **Test** tries the way to the CA from every member, **Renew** goes
    through the member that orders (or the Controller when it orders),
    an imported account key goes to every member.
  - A newer version waiting to be applied is named: you choose to start
    from it or from the members' version (409 in the API, `-base` for
    janusctl) - it is no longer left aside silently.
- **A configuration keepalived or BIRD refuses fails the apply**
  ([#648](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/648)), with their
  message, before any member is touched - found by the Proxmox proof.
- **An apply skips what a member already has**
  ([#645](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/645)): HAProxy's
  configuration to the byte, the firewall, VRRP and BGP modules,
  Let's Encrypt; a changed file still reloads HAProxy.

## 🌐 Network

- **Addresses announced when added**
  ([#647](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/647),
  [Applying a change](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/network-configuration.md#applying-a-change-trial-confirm-or-revert)):
  each address the node adds - a change, a revert, a DHCP lease - is
  announced three times a second apart, a gratuitous ARP for IPv4 and
  an unsolicited Neighbour Advertisement for IPv6 once duplicate
  address detection is over. The router and the cluster's other members
  take the node's MAC at once, instead of keeping the previous holder's.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Cold start with GitHub very slow**
  ([#642](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/642),
  [#646](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/646), fixes
  [#627](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/627)): the release list
  is read once, in the background, for every caller, with 3 minutes for
  a cold start; the small files of the newest release, the pre-release
  and the maintenance releases are read together; a list GitHub cuts
  short is read again at once; answers carry the `security.json` read
  so far.
  - Measured against GitHub at 4 s per request: the newest release
    known after 70 s and the 🔒 badge after 86 s - before, a Controller
    started without its cache still knew nothing after 8 minutes.
  - The log's "the list read … ago" says the list's real age.
- **Upload progress on a node's Update page**
  ([#642](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/642)): the file being
  sent, its bytes and a bar, then "files sent" and the node's own
  messages.

## 🛡️ SELinux

- janusd may stat init's and shutdown's executables: listing `/sbin`
  showed them as "permission denied" and logged two denials
  ([#641](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/641), fixes
  [#640](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/640)). Their content
  stays out of reach.

## 📦 Components

- **AWS-LC 5.14.0** (was 5.12.0) for HAProxy

  nftables, qemu-guest-agent), golang.org/x/crypto 0.59.0 and x/term
